newsitem.title: ALBANIA: GRENADE THROWN AT ALBANIAN PRESIDENT, TV SHOWS.
newsitem.headline: GRENADE THROWN AT ALBANIAN PRESIDENT, TV SHOWS.

text.p: A hand grenade was thrown at Albanian President Sali Berisha on Wednesday during an election campaign rally but failed to explode, state television showed.
The television said an assassination attempt was made at 18:20 p.m. (1620 GMT) while Berisha was speaking in the village of Shkallnuer, about 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana near the port of Durres.
A statement from Berisha's Democratic Party said the device thrown at Berisha as he spoke to a crowd of several hundred people was a grenade.
A suspect, identified as Ilir Ceta, 26, from a village near Durres, was captured and was being treated in hospital, the television said. It showed him with severe bruises on his face.
Berisha denounced the attempt as "an ugly act with which the terrorists aimed to take the lives of as many people as possible".

The incident came just two days after 20 people were wounded in a powerful blast at a Tirana cafe frequented by followers of the Socialist Party, which represents the biggest challenge to Berisha's party in June 29 elections.

The early elections were called after Albania was swept by riots last March sparked by the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes. Armouries were looted and it is estimated up to 1,000 people have been killed since in the Balkan state.
